literal: An edict cut off further memorials and granted the appointment at his home.
idiomatic: The court forbade further petitions and invested him at his residence.

literal: When the imperial carriage set out from Dai, Pi remained as guardian.
idiomatic: When the emperor left Dai, Pi stayed behind.

literal: An edict said that affairs in Dai were entirely entrusted to the Grand Tutor;
idiomatic: An edict entrusted everything in Dai to the Grand Tutor;

literal: He was given the emperor's own carriage and horses for going to and from the government offices.
idiomatic: He was granted the ruler's own carriage and horses for travel to and from the ministries.

literal: Pi dearly loved the old ways and did not grasp the new style.
idiomatic: Pi clung to the northern ways and did not grasp the new order.

literal: Changing customs and moving the capital to Luoyang, reforming offices and dress, and banning the old speech—all were unwelcome to him.
idiomatic: Sinicizing custom, moving the capital to Luoyang, changing offices and dress, and forbidding the old tongue—all of it displeased him.

literal: The emperor did not press him either, only guiding him with great principle so he would not breed dissent.
idiomatic: The emperor did not force him either, only setting out the larger rationale so he would not stir opposition.

literal: When court robes were already in use and vermilion dress filled the ranks, Pi still wore ordinary clothes seated at the corner.
idiomatic: Though court robes and scarlet ranks were already in use, Pi still sat in plain dress off to the side.

literal: Only later did he somewhat add cap and belt, but could not polish his bearing.
idiomatic: Only later did he add cap and belt a little, yet he never managed a polished appearance.

literal: The emperor, because Pi was aged and heavy-bodied, did not strongly demand it.
idiomatic: The emperor, seeing Pi's age and bulk, did not insist.

literal: When non-Emperor Daowu descendants and those of other surnames enfeoffed as kings were demoted, though reduced to dukes they still enjoyed fief revenues—Pi was displeased about this too.
idiomatic: When kings who were not Emperor Daowu's descendants or of other surnames were demoted, though cut to ducal rank they still kept fief income—Pi was unhappy even with that.

literal: When the emperor campaigned south, Pi memorialized begging to remain a while longer, planning again for a later effort.
idiomatic: During the emperor's southern campaign Pi asked leave to stay behind awhile, intending to try again later.

literal: When Minister over the Masses Feng Dan died, an edict ordered the six armies to turn their banners back.
idiomatic: When Minister Feng Dan died, an edict recalled the six armies.

literal: Pi also memorialized because Feng Xi had died at the Dai capital, requesting the imperial carriage attend in person.
idiomatic: Pi also memorialized that Feng Xi had died at Dai and begged the emperor to come in person.

literal: The edict said: "Luoyang is newly founded; eager hope and toil await completion.
idiomatic: The edict said: "Luoyang is only now rising; the realm waits on that labor.

literal: From the founding until now, how could one with the weight of the Son of Heaven travel far for a funeral in the maternal-kin state?
idiomatic: Since the founding, when has a Son of Heaven gone far away for a maternal uncle's mourning?

literal: Even if I wished to act as a filial son, what of the greater filial duty?
idiomatic: Even if I wished private filial piety, what of the greater filial duty to the realm?

literal: Even if I wished to act with righteousness, what of the greater righteousness?
idiomatic: Even if I wished private righteousness, what of the greater righteousness owed the state?

literal: The realm is paramount; the bond between ruler and minister is weighty—how can you lightly entice and lead the sovereign into unworthy conduct?
idiomatic: The empire outweighs all else; ruler and minister stand far apart—how can you coax the throne into discreditable conduct?

literal: The Director and Vice Director and those below may be handed to the judicial officers for demotion.
idiomatic: The Director, Vice Director, and their subordinates are to be referred to the judges for censure.

literal: An edict also appointed Pi commander-in-chief and governor of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He was also made area commander and given Bingzhou.

literal: Later an edict, because Pingyang lay in the capital district, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Xinxing.
idiomatic: Later, because Pingyang lay in the metropolitan belt, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xinxing.

literal: the corvée and tax labor of males of his registered household were released forever;
idiomatic: males of his household were forever freed from corvée and tax labor;

literal: Pi's sons by his first wife, Long and several full brothers, all lived apart.
idiomatic: Long and the other sons of Pi's first wife each kept separate households.

literal: Later he obtained palace women; those born to them shared one house and property.
idiomatic: Later palace women bore him children who lived together under one roof and shared the estate.

literal: Father-son affection was thus skewed.
idiomatic: Affection between father and sons was thereby skewed.

literal: Pi and his sons were broadly displeased with the move to Luoyang.
idiomatic: Pi and his sons were deeply unhappy about the transfer to Luoyang.

literal: When the emperor set out from Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun remained in the old capital.
idiomatic: When the emperor left Pingcheng, Crown Prince Xun stayed in the old capital.

literal: As he was about to return to Luoyang, Long and Mu Tai and others secretly plotted to keep Xun behind, then raised troops to hold the country north of Xiao.
idiomatic: On the return to Luoyang, Long and Mu Tai and others plotted to detain Xun and raised troops to seize the region north of Xiao.

literal: Pi's voice was high and clear; he remembered state affairs broadly; at banquets he always sat at the head and would raise his voice to speak at length, recounting past success and failure.
idiomatic: Pi spoke in a high, clear voice and remembered state affairs; at banquets he sat at the head and recounted past victories and defeats in a ringing voice.

literal: The emperor and empress listened with respect.
idiomatic: The emperor and empress listened with respect.

literal: Yet he flattered those in power and was arrogant toward the lowly; whenever he saw Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he would bend his body to place himself below them.
idiomatic: Yet he flattered the powerful and despised the lowly; before Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he bent low.

literal: Pi also followed the imperial progress to Pingcheng; at each interrogation he was made to sit and watch.
idiomatic: Pi followed the court to Pingcheng and was made to sit by while each interrogation proceeded.

literal: Together with the Yuan Ye brothers and the rest they were charged with plotting rebellion; the officials memorialized extermination to the third degree.
idiomatic: The Yuan Ye brothers and the rest were charged with treason; the court proposed exterminating their kin.

literal: Wang Rui, Director of the Masters of Writing, was ordered to proclaim the edict and grant Pi one golden seal-cord.
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rui proclaimed an edict granting Pi one golden seal-cord.

literal: Long and Chao's mother-born younger brothers and the remaining lesser brothers were all banished to Dunhuang.
idiomatic: The uterine brothers of Long and Chao and the other collateral kin were exiled to Dunhuang.

literal: The empress dowager ordered, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!
idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Ministers, neighbors! Neighbors, ministers!

literal: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.
idiomatic: The ruler must not idle above; ministers must walk on ice below.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, Pi came from Bing to attend; Emperor Xuanwu received him and, because Pi was an elder of the former reign, showed him added courtesy.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen died, Pi came from Bing to attend the funeral; Emperor Xuanwu received him and, as a survivor of the old court, showed him added respect.

literal: Soon he was ordered to remain in Luoyang.
idiomatic: He was soon ordered to stay in Luoyang.

literal: Later, at a banquet in the Hualin Pavilion, he was specially allowed two sons to support him in sitting and rising.
idiomatic: Later, at a feast in the Hualin Pavilion, two sons were specially assigned to help him sit and stand.

literal: Emperor the emperor and Empress Dowager Wenming received the dukes and ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust and the empress dowager said, "Now the capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let hungry and poor people leave the passes to seek food elsewhere.
idiomatic: the emperor and Wenming received the ministers in the Hall of Imperial Trust; the empress dowager said, "The capital suffers drought and dearth; I wish to let the hungry poor leave the passes to seek food.

literal: If we issue travel permits I fear days will be lost and the disaster will not be relieved; if we let them go freely I again fear good and wicked will be hard to tell apart.
idiomatic: Travel permits may cost days we do not have; free departure may mix honest folk with rogues.

literal: In Jingming year 4 he died, aged eighty-two.
idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 4 at eighty-two.

literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and regional inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Ping.
idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Left Grand Master of Splendid Service and inspector of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Ping.

literal: His eldest son Long had earlier been executed for rebellion.
idiomatic: His eldest son Long had already been executed for rebellion.

literal: Long's younger brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed together.
idiomatic: Long's brothers Yisheng and Chao were executed with him.

literal: Chao's younger brothers Jun and Yong both had military merit; Jun was enfeoffed Baron of Xin'an, Yong Baron of Jing.
idiomatic: Chao's brothers Jun and Yong both won military merit; Jun was made Baron of Xin'an and Yong Baron of Jing.

literal: Marquis Datou of Huailing was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: Datou, Marquis of Huailing, was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

literal: Skilled in mounted archery, he was promoted to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.
idiomatic: Skilled in mounted archery, he rose to Inner Third-Rank Gentleman.

literal: At the start of Emperor Emperor Wencheng's reign he was enfeoffed Huailing.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Emperor Wencheng's reign he was enfeoffed at Huailing.

literal: By nature cautious and reserved, the emperor valued him highly; he was made General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: Careful and discreet by nature, he was greatly esteemed and made General Who Pacifies the North.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping, with the posthumous title Lie.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously made Duke of Gaoping with the posthumous name Lie.

literal: Duke Qi of Hejian was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: Qi, Duke of Hejian, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Lie.

literal: Yu is Our splendid younger brother, gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.
idiomatic: Yu is Our splendid younger brother—gentle, warm, clear, and decisive.

literal: Emperor Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang.
idiomatic: Emperor Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang.

literal: Emperor Emperor Taiwu's horse stumbled and the enemy pressed the emperor.
idiomatic: The emperor's horse stumbled and the enemy closed in on him.

literal: Qi shielded him with his body, fought to the death, and the enemy withdrew so the emperor could remount.
idiomatic: Qi covered him with his body, fought as if to die, the enemy fell back, and the emperor remounted.

literal: Yu replied, "The Grand Commandant should hold sole command; your servant can only be second."
idiomatic: Yu answered, "The Grand Commandant should command alone; I can only assist."

literal: Emperor the emperor said, "The old have wisdom; the young have decision—how can you decline?"
idiomatic: the emperor said, "The old have wisdom, the young decision—how can you decline?"

literal: Once inside the city was alerted and every gate was shut.
idiomatic: The city soon discovered them and every gate was shut.

literal: The emperor and Qi and the others then entered the palace, obtained a woman's skirt, and tied it to a spear.
idiomatic: The emperor and Qi entered the palace, took a woman's skirt, and lashed it to a spear.

literal: The emperor climbed it and thus escaped; Qi had strength in this.
idiomatic: The emperor climbed out on it and escaped; Qi had the strength for that.

literal: He was granted the marquisate of Fuyang.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang.

literal: On the campaign against Helong he was appointed Master of Writing for merit and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he was made Master of Writing for merit and raised to duke.

literal: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba advanced and said, "The matter of moving the capital is great; in this servant's foolish view it cannot yet be done."
idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Yanzhou Mu Ba said, "Moving the capital is great; in my foolish view it cannot yet be done."

literal: Emperor the emperor said, "Then speak the reasons it cannot be done."
idiomatic: the emperor said, "Speak the reasons it cannot be done."

literal: Ba said, "In the north are the Xianyun raiders; in the south Jing and Yang are not yet submitted; in the west Tuyuhun blocks the way; in the east Koguryo is hard to overcome.
idiomatic: Ba said, "North are Xianyun raiders; south Jing and Yang are unsubmitted; west Tuyuhun blocks; east Koguryo is hard.

literal: The four quarters are not yet pacified; the nine regions are not yet settled.
idiomatic: The four quarters are not pacified; the nine regions unsettled.

literal: From this I infer it cannot be done."
idiomatic: From this I infer it cannot be done."

literal: Campaigns require war-horses; without horses affairs cannot succeed."
idiomatic: Campaigns need war-horses; without horses nothing succeeds."

literal: Emperor the emperor said, "Your saying there are no horses is roughly acceptable.
idiomatic: the emperor said, "Your point about horses is roughly acceptable.

literal: Horses always come from the north; the stud is placed here—why worry there will be no horses?
idiomatic: Horses come from the north; the stud is here—why fear there will be none?

literal: Now Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for this reason We move to the central plain."
idiomatic: Dai lies north of Mount Heng, outside the Nine Provinces; for that We move to the central plain."

literal: Ba said, "I have heard that the Yellow Emperor's capital was at Zhuolu.
idiomatic: Ba said, "I hear the Yellow Emperor's capital was Zhuolu.

literal: From this, ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."
idiomatic: So ancient sage kings did not all dwell in the central plain."

literal: For merit he was appointed Grand Inner Steward.
idiomatic: For this merit he was made Grand Inner Steward.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "Your servant truly does not know ancient affairs; as I hear the common people speak, the late emperor built the capital here—suddenly to move, they think it cannot be done.
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Guo said: [12] "I truly do not know antiquity; as the people say, the late emperor built here—to move suddenly they think cannot be done.

literal: His eldest son Ling inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eldest son Ling succeeded to the title.

literal: Ling was upright and unyielding; in the first year of Tian'an he was killed by Yihun.
idiomatic: Ling was blunt and unyielding; in Tian'an year 1 Yihun killed him.

literal: Ling's younger brother Lan was favored for loyalty and prudence.
idiomatic: Ling's brother Lan won favor for loyalty and care.

literal: Your servant's shallow tube-view and nature not bright and penetrating would never compare the land of Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.
idiomatic: My shallow sight would never compare Heng and Dai to the beauty of Yiluo.

literal: His son Zhi, styled Menglue, in youth was clear in debate and strong in execution; he read widely in books and records and had considerable literary talent.
idiomatic: His son Zhi, styled Menglue, was sharp in debate and forceful in action as a youth, widely read, and gifted in letters.

literal: He was made magistrate of Luoyang and did not yield to the powerful; he and Censor-in-Chief Li Biao disputed the road and both entered audience.
idiomatic: As magistrate of Luoyang he did not yield to the powerful; he and Censor-in-Chief Li Biao clashed over precedence and both went in to audience.

literal: When I first received the gracious command my heart was anxious and unsettled.
idiomatic: When I first received the command my heart was anxious.

literal: Whenever one wishes to migrate one should consult divination by milfoil and tortoise and determine fortune or ill fortune—only then may one act."
idiomatic: Any migration should ask the milfoil and tortoise and fix fortune or ill fortune—only then act."

literal: Emperor the emperor said to Pi, "Formerly at Ye, Duke of Works Dan, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong all wished to request tortoise divination for the fortune of moving to Luo.
idiomatic: the emperor said to Pi, "At Ye, Dan Duke of Works, Xi Prince of Xianyang, and Li Chong all wished to divine moving to Luo.

literal: I then told Dan and the others that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined the site at Yiluo and so knew the utmost omen.
idiomatic: I told them that in antiquity the Duke of Zhou divined Yiluo and knew the utmost omen.

literal: Now there is no one like him; divination is also of no use.
idiomatic: Now there is no one like him; divination is useless.

literal: On leaving, he and Biao measured the road with a folding rule and each took half.
idiomatic: Outside, he and Biao measured the street with a folding rule and each took half.

literal: Formerly when Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked to consult the worthy; Xuanyuan then asked Tian Lao, and Tian Lao said it was good.
idiomatic: When Xuanyuan divined, the tortoise scorched; the diviner asked the wise; Xuanyuan asked Tian Lao, who said it was good.

literal: Yan said: "Bamboo in dew and frost has many tough joints;
idiomatic: Yan said: "Bamboo in dew and frost has many tough joints;

literal: if it is not a luan it is a phoenix—the stock is the source."
idiomatic: if it is not a luan it is a phoenix—the lineage shows in the branch."

literal: Staff member Feng Jun, younger brother of Lady Zhaoyi, relied on his backing to beat the village headmen under him at will.
idiomatic: Feng Jun, an outer-office attendant and brother of Lady Zhaoyi, bullied the village heads in his district at will.

literal: For the people who move south I myself will pile storehouses high so they will not suffer want."
idiomatic: For those who move south I will pile storehouses so they do not suffer want."

literal: For this he offended the throne and was demoted to secretary of the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: This offended the throne and he was demoted to secretary under the Grand Commandant.

literal: Soon he was made Attendant Gentleman.
idiomatic: He was soon made Attendant Gentleman.

literal: Formerly Emperor Pingwen abandoned his back to the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built his dwelling at Shengle;
idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen turned his back on the realm; Emperor Zhaocheng built at Shengle;

literal: Emperor Daowu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved his dwelling to Pingcheng.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu Daowu by divine martiality answered Heaven and moved to Pingcheng.

literal: The arrow struck Zhi in the eye, and he lost sight in that eye.
idiomatic: The shaft struck Zhi's eye, and he lost sight in it.
